title: Chapter 47
content:
Buttoning his crisp dress shirt before the full-length mirror, Kang Il-hyun glanced at the timepiece resting on the dresser shelf.

It was the luxury watch he had buckled onto Lee Ja-kyeong’s wrist the previous evening—the one outfitted with an encrypted listening bug. He hadn't anticipated the kid prying the casing apart so effortlessly. He had written the boy off as a clumsy, docile amateur playing a role, but it seemed the stray cat possessed sharper claws than expected.

Snapping his cufflinks into place, Il-hyun pulled on his tailored suit jacket and stepped out of his master suite.

In the open foyer below, the senior housekeeper was methodically stacking the morning newspapers.

"Heading out so early, Executive Director?"

"Yes. I'll take breakfast at headquarters."

Il-hyun paused at the base of the central staircase. Whether the boy was naturally a heavy sleeper or simply exhausted, Ja-kyeong never emerged before noon. And after last night's relentless exertion—having pushed him through several grueling rounds until dawn—he was bound to be completely spent.

"Ensure Master Yi-an’s meals are prepared with extra care today," Il-hyun instructed smoothly. "Something rich in protein and nutrients."

"Of course, sir. Leave it to me."

Offering a polite nod, Il-hyun stepped out into the crisp morning air. Over by the courtyard terrace, maintenance workers were draining the pool basin. Last night's torrential rain had muddied the water, and the filtration system had choked on debris; an outside servicing team was scheduled to inspect the pumps this afternoon.

Waiting outside the main gates, Park Tae-soo was already idling the black luxury sedan.

Il-hyun slid into the rear leather seat, and the vehicle glided down the mountain road. From the front passenger seat, Tae-soo turned around, passing a leather-bound briefing folder over the console.

"The confirmed dignitary roster for the upcoming inauguration ceremony, sir."

Opening the file, Chairman Kang Hoon’s name was listed at the very top of the VIP index, followed by Kang Yu-jung, extended family members, key National Assembly lawmakers, senior prosecutors, and board executives.

The contract parameters were precise: Lee Ja-kyeong was scheduled to take the shot the moment Il-hyun concluded his formal inauguration address.

Scanning the names, Tae-soo spoke in a quiet, measured cadence. "Once the operation concludes... how should we handle Lee Ja-kyeong?"

Il-hyun’s fingers paused over the parchment. After a beat of cold deliberation, he delivered the verdict in a flat, uninflected monotone.

"Eliminate him immediately."

In the rearview mirror, Tae-soo’s stoic brow twitched with faint surprise. Despite keeping their distance during the day, anyone with eyes could tell the dynamic between the Director and the boy had crossed far beyond professional boundaries. Whispers were already circulating among the domestic staff.

Il-hyun lifted his chin, his dark pupils locking onto Tae-soo's eyes in the glass.

"What is with that look?"

Tae-soo lowered his gaze instantly. "My apologies, sir."

"If Lee Ja-kyeong draws breath after the dust settles, it creates unnecessary complications for the old man—and twice as many for me. Clean him up without exception."

"Understood, Director."

Il-hyun shifted his gaze toward the passing forest.

The memory of Ja-kyeong’s flushed, unraveling face beneath him flashed vividly in his mind. The sight of those dark eyes welling with heat, glaring up with that venomous, desperate defiance... it was an image that would linger in his thoughts long after the boy was gone. But leaving a potential liability alive—no matter how enticing—was a mistake he never made.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, sir?"

"Don't just dump his corpse in some ditch. Bury him properly."

"Understood."

Closing the dossier, Il-hyun tossed it onto the empty leather seat beside him. He reclined against the headrest, closing his eyes.

Unbidden, the boy's features materialized once more behind his lids: the smooth pale curve of his neck, the swollen lips he’d bitten to choke back his cries, the burning crimson ears, the dark, devastatingly alluring eyes that turned feverish with pleasure...

Perhaps... instead of burying him in the cold dirt, I should have him taxidermied.

Standing in his briefs before the bathroom vanity, Jakyeong let out a dry, incredulous scoff.

His lower back throbbed so brutally he could barely stand straight, every muscle aching as though he’d been run over by an industrial roller. His chest was so tender and inflamed that merely brushing against it wrenched a sharp gasp from his throat, forcing him to apply soothing balm and fresh medical tape over the raw tissue.

Muttering a string of foul curses, he plastered medicated pain patches across his flanks and shoulders before shuffling back into the bedroom. Every step drew a low, involuntary wince.

Dropping to his knees, he unlocked the floor safe beneath the bed and retrieved the USB flash drive he had lifted from Il-hyun's Seoul penthouse.

Pacing the room with the drive in hand, he powered on his laptop and inserted the stick.

Scanning the storage partition, his jaw clamped shut. The drive was completely blank—a sanitized, empty decoy.

I knew it.

His instincts hadn't failed him. There was no way a paranoid syndicate boss would leave catastrophic corporate blackmail sitting in an unlocked penthouse devoid of active CCTV cameras. Ejecting the useless drive, he shoved it into his pocket instead of the safe.

He headed downstairs. Passing a few domestic staff in the corridor, he noticed the senior housekeeper was nowhere to be found, though a rich, savory aroma was drifting from the industrial kitchen. Needing fresh air to clear the mental static, he stepped outside.

The afternoon sun was blazing high in the sky. Cleared by the storm, the atmosphere was pristine, a vibrant azure dome spanning the horizon. Stretching his stiff arms overhead, he strolled across the damp lawn; the gentle movement actually helped ease the dull ache in his joints.

His encrypted burner phone buzzed in his pocket.

[7.5 million USD confirmed in escrow.]

It was the wire from Kang Il-hyun—roughly nine billion won. Combined with the initial advance from Chairman Kang, the total bounty climbed to twelve billion won. The father and son had started from opposite sides of the board, but their end goal was identical: putting a bullet in each other.

Walking toward the rear courtyard, muffled voices drew his attention.

Rounding the stone annex, he found the senior housekeeper leaning on a garden spade, methodically tamping down a patch of fresh earth. Beside her sat the German Shepherd, panting happily with its tail sweeping across the grass.

"What are you doing out here, ma'am?"

She turned around, dabbing a bead of sweat from her brow with the back of her wrist, offering a warm maternal smile. "Happy was parading around with something rather gruesome in his jaws, so I came out to bury it."

Jakyeong blinked. Happy?

Naming a vicious, throat-tearing attack dog "Happy" was delightfully absurd.

The housekeeper picked up an open bottle of liquor and poured a slow libation over the fresh mound. Jakyeong had zero doubt that resting beneath that soil was the mangled head of Choi Ki-tae.

When the hound nudged the dirt with its snout, she issued a crisp, stern command: "No." The beast understood the tone immediately, dropping its ears and trotting obediently toward the shade.

"You should have let the groundskeepers handle that..."

"Whoever has free hands should do the chores," she chuckled, gently nudging Jakyeong toward the house with the handle of the spade. "Come inside—you've just woken up, so you must be famished."

Guided into the dining room, the sheer scale of the lunch spread left Jakyeong stunned. The mahogany table was laden with premium seared beef dishes, rich stews, and roasted sides that made his mouth water on the spot.

"Is today a special occasion?"

"You've seemed drained lately, so I prepared something hearty."

"Please, sit and join me."

"I've already eaten, dear. Actually, the Executive Director called before leaving this morning, specifically requesting that I look after your nutrition since you seemed low on energy."

"Ah... I see..."

"He has such a thoughtful heart beneath that stern face."

She beamed with open pride. Hearing the man who had brutally drained his energy framed as a "thoughtful gentleman" was surreal. Giving someone a disease just to hand them the cure. Jakyeong felt a chaotic tangle of resentment, begrudging appreciation, and lingering confusion over last night's intimacy.

Polishing off the meal, he stepped out into the living room, noticing figures still moving around the pool terrace.

The housekeeper mentioned they were a contracted technical crew repairing the pump filters damaged in the storm. Yet watching them through the floor-to-ceiling glass, their furtive glances and rigid postures set every tactical alarm ringing.

Jakyeong scanned the coffee table, smoothly palming a heavy metal fountain pen and sliding it up his sleeve before walking outside.

As he crossed the manicured lawn, the guard by the front gate glanced his way. Jakyeong approached the poolside coping.

Two men in generic maintenance overalls were pouring liquid chemical additive into the freshly filled basin. The worker holding the plastic drum glanced up, offering a tight, perfunctory bow.

"Is the maintenance nearly finished?"

"Yes, sir. The basin should be completely filled by evening."

"That's a relief... I was hoping to go for a swim today."

Jakyeong stepped closer, inspecting the chemical drum. "What chemical is that?"

"Industrial pool disinfectant, sir."

"Do you mind if I catch a scent?"

The man's shoulders locked with sudden tension. Crouching beside the drum, Jakyeong tilted his head, studying the worker's rigid profile with an unblinking gaze.

"May I?"

The worker turned his head slowly, forcing a strained, unnatural smile. "It's just standard chlorine, sir... The fumes are quite toxic and harsh on the respiratory system."

"If it's that toxic, is it safe to dump directly into a residential pool?"

The man stammered out a vague excuse, averting his eyes.

Jakyeong rose to his feet. Across the basin, the second maintenance worker was tracking his movements with intense focus. Those eyes are familiar.

Jakyeong shifted his weight, feigning a clumsy stumble and driving his shoulder hard into the first worker's back.

Losing his balance, the man plunged headfirst into the knee-deep water.

The worker scrambled frantically to his feet, desperate to crawl out of the basin—only to clamp both hands around his own throat, letting out strangled, choking gasps as thick white foam bubbled from his lips. He dragged himself onto the stone coping, writhing in violent convulsions as the acidic agent seared his airway.

Across the pool, the second man reached beneath his overalls, whipping out a heavy combat knife.

"You fucking bastard!"

The face clicked instantly: one of Choi Ki-tae's inner-circle enforcers from the offshore yacht.

As the thug charged with the blade raised, Jakyeong whipped the heavy fountain pen from his sleeve, popped the cap, and hurled the steel casing with pinpoint ballistic precision.

The tungsten nib buried itself deep into the man's right eye socket.

A blood-curdling shriek shattered the afternoon quiet as the thug collapsed, clawing at his ruined eye, just as the estate's armed security detail came sprinting across the lawn.
